about: Sixteen cards written 2026-11-27 by a Claude session following tools/combo-cards/BRIEF.md: the next most-used missing pairs of the NAME chart (a center with the aura beside it, a center's main and sub vibration, two auras side by side).

cards.position: They think fast, speak their mind clearly and come across as lively and successful (14/5). What strangers and the public conclude is someone strong and a little intimidating, who sets firm limits (9).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both are quick, masculine, outgoing numbers (14/5, 9). Neither waits to be asked.

course.text: "It makes people who approach you for the first time feel a strong and perhaps slightly intimidating energy that is not to be trifled with."

reasoning: The owner's phrase for 5 with 9 is "direct communication": talkative and good at it (14/5), with a number that is bold and outright (9).
The public meets the firmness first (9). The friendliness comes once they start talking (14/5).
The combo guide warns that a hard number beside a 5 turns it to harsh selling: the message (14/5) is pushed too hard (9).
cards.best: Says clearly what they mean (14/5) and is taken seriously (9).
cards.worst: Talks over people (14/5) in a tone that frightens them off (9).

phrases: The Head That Will Not Stop
cards.position: Inside they turn things over in the head, feel misunderstood and read other people's intentions wrongly (12/3), with a tint of exactly the same (12/3).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Everything: it is the same number twice. The overthinking and the feeling of being wronged are both doubled (12/3, 12/3).

course.about: 12/3 twice in a center (written for the mind center)
course.text: "Too much 12/3 in the mind center helps to reinforce the unhappy aspects of 12/3. One feels deeply misunderstood and victimized in ones communication with others."

reasoning: A sub vibration usually tints the main one with something else. Here it tints it with more of itself (12/3, 12/3).
Loved ones cannot read them (12/3), and they do not read loved ones correctly either (12/3).
In love they are sure they give more than they get (12/3), and the partner is just as sure of the opposite (12/3).
cards.best: Thinks a feeling through until they truly understand it (12/3) and can explain it to others (12/3).
cards.worst: Takes a partner's harmless remark the wrong way (12/3) and broods on it for days (12/3).

phrases: Sunny at Home, Hard on Themselves
cards.position: Inside they are driven and hard on themselves, with a harsh inner voice (9). What a partner and family see is a strong, cheerful person who fills the home with enthusiasm (10/1).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both give out and neither takes in: 9 pushes (9), 10/1 shines (10/1).

course.text: "You are likely to be loved because you fill those around you with enthusiasm, joy and happiness."

reasoning: The family sees the optimism (10/1) and does not hear the voice that tells them they are not doing well enough (9).
10/1 turns up what stands beside it (10/1), so the inner critic is louder for it (9).
They lead and provide at home (10/1, 9) and find it hard to be the one who is comforted.
cards.best: Carries the family with strength (9) and good cheer (10/1).
cards.worst: Acts as if everything is fine (10/1) while tearing into themselves inside (9).

cards.position: Inside they are lively and want movement, talk and contact (14/5), with a tint of force and a harsh inner voice (9).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both are quick, masculine numbers that go outward (14/5, 9).

course.text: "gives very strong and direct communication. It also gives skills in sales, marketing and branding. In imbalance there is a tendency to be harsh in one's communication and to over-sell"

reasoning: 14/5 is the main one: they talk their feelings out easily (14/5). The 9 makes what they say blunt (9).
The same passage says they can talk too much (14/5) and be bossy with a partner or children (9).
They get restless at home (14/5) and blame themselves for it (9).
cards.best: Tells a loved one the truth (9) in words that are easy to hear (14/5).
cards.worst: Talks a partner down (14/5) until they give in (9).

phrases: Hard on Colleagues, Harder on Themselves
cards.position: Inside they are hard on themselves to an extreme, with anger shut in until it bursts (18/9). What colleagues and acquaintances see is someone strong-willed, direct and tough (9).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both are nines, and 18/9 is the harsher one (18/9, 9). The hardness is doubled.

course.text: "colleagues may see you as a slightly repressed person who is very hard on yourself."

reasoning: Colleagues read them correctly: the toughness outside (9) is the toughness inside, only more so (18/9).
They ask a lot of colleagues (9) and far more of themselves (18/9).
The associates aura text says an over-provoked 9 explodes. With 18/9 behind it, the fuse is shorter.
cards.best: Leads a team by working harder than anyone on it (18/9) and saying plainly what is needed (9).
cards.worst: Holds it in at work until it bursts (18/9), and a colleague takes the blast (9).

phrases: Same at Work and at Home
cards.position: What colleagues and acquaintances see is someone strong-willed, direct and tough (9). What a partner and family see is the same: strong, direct and quick-tempered (9).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Everything: it is the same number twice. Nobody, at work or at home, gets a softer version (9, 9).

course.text: "it will help colleagues and acquaintances not by “giving them fish”, but by teaching them to fish, so that they can awaken their own inner strength and resourcefulness."

reasoning: They treat family like a team (9) and a team like family (9): direct, demanding, loyal.
Neither aura shields the emotion center (9, 9). What they feel shows as force on both sides.
Two 9 auras add up to an emotion center 18/9, so the hardness they show is harder still inside.
cards.best: Stands up for colleagues (9) and for family (9) alike.
cards.worst: Is blunt at work (9) and blunt at home (9), and wonders why people keep their distance.
cards.made: Made together: the emotion center 18/9, anger shut in until it bursts.

cards.position: Inside they run on attraction: charm, desire and wanting to be wanted (15/6). What colleagues and acquaintances see is someone thoughtful, creative and well liked, with a touch of mystery (7).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both are loved, feminine numbers (15/6, 7). The combo guide says a 7 lifts 15/6.

course.text: "a strong and hypnotic charisma that fascinates people and gives an aura of sensuality and mystery."

reasoning: The 7 aura keeps the desire (15/6) out of sight at work: colleagues see depth and calm (7).
They do not push for attention among colleagues (7), which makes people more curious about them (15/6).
A 7 aura leaves the center open. If it slips, colleagues see the drama (15/6) with nothing in front of it (7).
cards.best: Draws colleagues in (15/6) with ideas worth their time (7).
cards.worst: Charms a colleague (15/6) and then goes distant on them (7).

phrases: Open at Work, Guarded at Home
cards.position: What colleagues and acquaintances see is someone thoughtful, creative and well liked (7). What a partner and family see is someone strong and careful, who keeps watch over them and keeps a little distance (8).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both keep some distance: 7 by drifting off into thought (7), 8 by holding people back on purpose (8).

course.text: "you can also have subtle rings around you - where you never let those closest to you get too close."

reasoning: Colleagues find them easier to be with (7) than the family does (8).
At work they explore ideas freely (7). At home they keep order and remember who did what (8).
The course's line for an 8 aura beside a 7 is that the 8 grounds the 7's insight: their intuition about people (7) is put to use protecting the family (8).
cards.best: Is open-minded with colleagues (7) and fiercely loyal at home (8).
cards.worst: Gives acquaintances their best side (7) and the family their strictest (8).
cards.made: Made together: the emotion center 15/6, charm and wanting to be wanted.

cards.position: Inside they are controlled, tough and stubborn, and keep a mask on (8), with a tint of overthinking and feeling misunderstood (12/3).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both keep count: 8 remembers every wrong (8), 12/3 feels every slight (12/3).

course.about: 8 and 12/3 together in a center (written for the mind center)
course.text: "give a low self-esteem where there is a tendency to always doubt one's actions. Every time you set something in motion, you immediately doubt it and pull back."

reasoning: 8 is the main one: they look composed (8). The doubt is a tint that only they hear (12/3).
The same passage: loved ones come to them for advice (8), and they are left tired and feeling used (12/3).
They keep score at home (8) and feel the balance is always against them (12/3).
cards.best: Takes responsibility for the family (8) and thinks each decision through (12/3).
cards.worst: Controls a partner (8) and feels like the wronged one when the partner objects (12/3).

cards.position: Inside they are controlled, tough and stubborn, and keep a mask on (8), with a tint of charm and wanting to be wanted (15/6).

share.title: What Sets Them Apart
share.text: 8 is duty and control (8). 15/6 is desire and attraction (15/6). Lecture: 6 likes 8.

course.text: "can give psychopathic tendencies where you coolly are able to exploit other people."

reasoning: 8 is the main one, so control comes first (8). The 15/6 gives the control a charming face (15/6).
They keep their own feelings locked away (8) and read a partner's easily (15/6).
The combo guide's balanced reading of the pair is psychological insight: someone who sees what a person wants (15/6) and handles it responsibly (8).
cards.best: Stays calm in a family crisis (8) and knows what each person needs to hear (15/6).
cards.worst: Shows a partner just enough warmth (15/6) to keep the upper hand (8).

cards.position: Inside they run on attraction: charm, desire and wanting to be wanted (15/6). What colleagues and acquaintances see is someone loving and likable, who finds the harmonious solution (6).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both are sixes: love and attraction (15/6, 6). 15/6 is the 6 that makes drama. The theme is doubled.

course.text: "No matter how you feel in your solar plexus center, you will try to be loving and have loving communication with your colleagues."

reasoning: The 6 aura shields the center: colleagues get the pleasant side (6), and the craving stays private (15/6).
They are popular at work (6) and still need more proof that they are wanted (15/6).
With love on both sides (15/6, 6), a workplace friendship easily turns into a flirtation.
cards.best: Makes a workplace pleasant (6) and is warmly liked for it (15/6).
cards.worst: Keeps colleagues charmed (6) because they cannot stand not being wanted (15/6).

cards.position: Inside they are warm, feel good about themselves and are at home in closeness (6), with a tint of overthinking and feeling taken for granted (12/3).

share.title: What Sets Them Apart
share.text: 6 feels at home with people (6). 12/3 feels misunderstood by them (12/3).

course.text: "You can feel like you're giving and giving, but it's never good enough and you never get anything in return, leaving you feeling tired, burned out and unappreciated."

reasoning: 6 is the main one, so love basically works for them (6). The 12/3 is a tint at the edges (12/3).
Their care (6) gets misread (12/3).
The same passage says they feel like a victim of other people's drama while helping to create it in ways they cannot see (12/3).
cards.best: Loves their family (6) and learns from each misunderstanding how the others think (12/3).
cards.worst: Does a kindness nobody asked for (6) and is hurt when it is not noticed (12/3).

cards.position: They think with bright optimism and come across as cheerful, lucky and youthful (10/1). What friends see is someone strong and independent, who helps by making them stronger (9).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both give out and neither takes in: 10/1 shines (10/1), 9 pushes (9). The course's word for 9 with 1 is megalomania.

course.text: "you would probably help your friends not by “giving them fish”, but by teaching them to fish"

reasoning: 10/1 turns up what stands beside it (10/1), so friends get the 9 at full strength: the honesty and the push (9).
They believe in a friend's chances (10/1) and tell them bluntly what to do about it (9).
They give friends a great deal of energy (10/1) and seldom ask a friend for help (9).
cards.best: Makes a friend believe they can do it (10/1) and holds them to it (9).
cards.worst: Is sure they know best (10/1) and tells friends so without being asked (9).

phrases: Winner in Public, Fighter Among Friends
cards.position: What strangers and the public conclude is a strong person with a winner's attitude (10/1). What friends see is someone strong and independent, who helps by making them stronger (9).

share.title: What They Share
share.text: Both are strong, masculine numbers that give out (10/1, 9). Neither aura shows a soft side.

course.text: "10/1 in this aura provides good protection for the heart center, meaning that you will not be easily swayed by public opinion"

reasoning: The public and friends agree about them: strong (10/1, 9). Only the tone differs, sunny for strangers (10/1) and blunt for friends (9).
They are hard to sway (10/1) and hard to argue with (9).
Whatever doubt they have stays in the mind center between the two auras, where neither the public nor friends see it (10/1, 9).
cards.best: Wins the public's confidence (10/1) and their friends' respect (9).
cards.worst: Comes across as full of themselves in public (10/1) and bossy with friends (9).
cards.made: Made together: the mind center 10/1, bright, optimistic thinking.

phrases: Wanted, and Sure They Are Not
cards.position: Inside they run on attraction: charm, desire and wanting to be wanted (15/6), with a tint of overthinking and feeling wronged (12/3).

share.title: What Sets Them Apart
share.text: 15/6 knows how to be wanted (15/6). 12/3 doubts that it is (12/3).

course.text: "paranoia, you create vivid images about how people are out to get you"

reasoning: 15/6 is the main one: the pull toward people is strong (15/6). The 12/3 adds suspicion about what they want back (12/3).
The course says 15/6 turns to drama in relationships when the number beside it in the emotion center is one like 12/3.
They picture a partner's unfaithfulness in detail (12/3), and the picture feels as real as the love does (15/6).
cards.best: Loves intensely (15/6) and thinks hard about what makes a relationship work (12/3).
cards.worst: Imagines a slight from a partner (12/3) and makes a scene over it (15/6).

cards.position: Inside they are driven and hard on themselves, with a harsh inner voice (9), with a tint of charm and wanting to be wanted (15/6).

course.about: 15/6 and 9 in the emotion center, at its most balanced
course.text: "these numbers can create a strong polarity between masculine and feminine, and thus great attraction and sexual tension."

reasoning: 9 is the main one: the drive comes first (9), and the charm is how it gets what it wants (15/6).
The course's name for the pair is "the Player": partners are won (9) more than loved (15/6).
Being wanted (15/6) quiets the voice that says they are not good enough (9), for a while.
cards.best: Pursues the person they want with courage (9) and wins them with warmth (15/6).
